name: 'If it is said … I say' (fa-in qīla … qultu)
definition: The form of objection and answer in which the commentaries argue: the author raises the objection a reader might make and answers it.
body: A commentary does not only explain; it defends its text. 'If it is said…' (fa-in qīla) introduces an objection, 'I say' (qultu) or 'we say' (qulnā) the answer; 'one should not say…' (lā yuqālu) heads off a mistaken objection, and 'because we say' (li-annā naqūlu) gives the reason. The form goes back to the disputations of the schools and is the same in law and theology. Sharḥ Jāmī and its glosses are built of such exchanges, and the student learns to follow who is speaking.

examples.text: 'One should not say … because we say …'
